title: How I Actually Learned English: No Fancy Classes, Just Continuity
excerpt: A personal story of learning English from forced childhood classes to YouTube and computer engineering, where continuity mattered more than any fancy course.

blocks.text: I was 9 years old when my family forced me to go to English class. I remember exactly the day they told me they had signed me up. I cried. It felt strange, but it was really necessary. And I'll say it here: good for them for thinking about it back then.

From age 9 to 18, before the university entrance exam, I went to English class constantly and very regularly. Because these classes continued nonstop, my English gradually got better, and I never really had a serious problem with the language.
The first place it helped me a lot was the Konkur. For both my undergraduate and master's entrance exams, I never had a weakness in English, and that gave me a lot of confidence.

At 18, I decided to stop going to class. I really didn't want to keep going like that, doing the same simple grammar every term. I felt my biggest problem was that I couldn't speak well. And maybe I still had trouble with listening. I knew a lot, but I deeply felt I still couldn't communicate. Like in the real world, I couldn't connect.
An old friend suggested I go around and talk to foreigners. At that time, more tourists were coming to my country, Iran. But I didn't have enough confidence for that!

But I started watching YouTube. At first, I really didn't understand what these foreigners were saying, and understanding was very hard for me. But little by little, I learned. If I didn't understand a word or sentence, I would search for it and find the Persian meaning to learn it. But I won't lie to you, I didn't write anything down anywhere. But it was repeated so much that it stuck. This was where, over time, I felt my English was really getting better and I gained a better general understanding of the language.

At the same time, when I got accepted into computer engineering, I started watching many courses that were entirely in English. All the books, documentation, and everything else were in English. This continuity in watching and reading gradually improved my English.
In the end, I didn't use any complicated formula or a very strange class for my English. I think this sentence sums it up well:
Continuity was the best class I ever took to strengthen my English. :)
